issues.legal_issue: A development application cannot be rejected solely because revision of the development plan is contemplated when no draft revised plan or other concrete planning material exists.
material_facts: The sanctioned plan placed the land in a residential zone.
The landowner submitted a development plan for a hotel.
The Municipal Commissioner rejected the application solely because the land might be earmarked for recreation during a contemplated revision of the development plan.
No draft revised plan existed when the application was rejected.
issues.conclusion: The ground for rejecting the application was untenable, and the appellate authority was justified in allowing the appeal.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 45 and 46 of the Maharashtra Regional and Town Planning Act, 1966 require regard to relevant development plans and proposals published or sanctioned under the Act, but do not prevent consideration of other relevant material. A rejection must be supported by concrete material; a merely contemplated plan revision is insufficient. The Court distinguished Life Insurance Corporation of India v. Municipal Corporation of Greater Bombay, where a draft revised plan existed as relevant material.

rule.if: development_permission_appeal and application_for_development_submitted and refusal_based_only_on_future_plan_revision and no_existing_draft_plan and no_concrete_planning_material

predicates.development_permission_appeal: An applicant appealed the refusal of permission to develop land.
predicates.application_for_development_submitted: A landowner submitted a plan seeking permission to develop land.
predicates.refusal_based_only_on_future_plan_revisi: The planning authority relied solely on a possible future revision of its development plan to refuse permission.
predicates.no_existing_draft_plan: No draft revised development plan existed when the planning authority refused permission.
predicates.no_concrete_planning_material: The planning authority had no concrete planning material supporting its refusal.

issues.definition: When an applicant appeals a development refusal based only on a future plan revision and no draft plan or concrete supporting material exists, the refusal is unjustified.

issues.legal_issue: A planning authority's decision to revise a development plan does not by itself make an appeal against refusal of development permission incompetent.
material_facts: The Municipal Corporation had decided to revise the development plan.
The landowner had been refused development permission and appealed that refusal to the State Government.
issues.conclusion: The appeal under section 47 was competent; the planning authority's decision to revise the plan did not bar it.
issues.legal_principle: Section 47 of the Maharashtra Regional and Town Planning Act, 1966 provides an appeal to the State Government or its appointed officer for an applicant aggrieved by an order granting permission subject to conditions or refusing permission under section 45. Reading into section 47 a bar based on a decision to revise the plan would amount to rewriting the provision.

predicates.development_permission_appeal: An applicant pursued an appeal concerning a development-permission order.
predicates.applicant_aggrieved_by_permission_order: The applicant was aggrieved by an order refusing development permission or granting it subject to conditions.
predicates.planning_authority_decided_to_revise_pla: The planning authority had decided to revise its development plan.

issues.definition: An appeal by an applicant aggrieved by a development-permission order remains competent even if the planning authority has decided to revise its development plan.

issues.legal_issue: Conditional development approval is sustainable where its conditions reserve substantial land for public recreation and the approved plan accords with the published draft revised plan.
material_facts: The appellate authority directed approval subject to conditions reserving land for recreation or a green belt and requiring land set aside as green space to be taken over by the Municipal Commissioner.
After the conditions were applied, only part of the disputed land remained available for hotel construction.
A draft revised development plan was later published, and the conditionally approved plan was consistent with it.
There was no material showing that the Municipal Corporation prepared the draft revised plan under the appellate authority's direction, and the Corporation did not challenge the appellate order.
issues.conclusion: The appellate authority acted in the public interest, and the challenge to its conditional approval had no merit.
issues.legal_principle: The Court assessed the conditions imposed and the consistency of the approved plan with the subsequently published draft revised plan. It found no material supporting the claim that the planning authority had prepared that draft under the appellate authority's direction and noted that the planning authority had accepted the appellate order.

predicates.appeal_against_conditional_development_a: A proceeding challenged an appellate authority's conditional approval of a development plan.
predicates.substantial_land_reserved_for_public_rec: The approval's conditions set aside a substantial part of the land for recreation or green space.
predicates.approved_plan_consistent_with_published_: The conditionally approved plan was consistent with a subsequently published draft revised plan.
predicates.no_evidence_draft_followed_appellate_dir: The record contained no material showing that the planning authority prepared the draft revised plan pursuant to the appellate authority's direction.
predicates.planning_authority_did_not_challenge_app: The planning authority accepted the appellate order and did not challenge it.

issues.definition: A conditional development approval is upheld when it reserves substantial land for public recreation, accords with the published draft plan, and is not shown to have procured that draft through the appellate authority's direction, particularly where the planning authority did not challenge the approval.

issues.legal_issue: A challenge to a land-reservation resolution is no longer tenable when a subsequently published draft revised plan is consistent with the conditionally approved development plan.
material_facts: A municipal resolution modified the park reservation to cover a limited part of the disputed land.
A draft revised development plan was subsequently published.
The plan approved subject to conditions was not inconsistent with the published draft revised plan.
The petitioners did not seriously press the challenge to the resolution.
issues.conclusion: The challenge to the resolution was no longer tenable, and the special leave petition was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: The Court relied on the subsequent publication of the draft revised development plan and its consistency with the conditionally approved plan in concluding that the challenge to the resolution was no longer tenable.

predicates.resolution_challenge_in_special_leave_pr: A special leave proceeding challenged a resolution concerning reservation of land for a public park.
predicates.later_draft_plan_published: A draft revised development plan was published after the resolution was made.
predicates.conditionally_approved_plan_consistent_w: The development plan approved subject to conditions was consistent with the published draft revised plan.

issues.definition: A challenge to a land-reservation resolution is rejected as no longer tenable when a later-published draft plan is consistent with the conditionally approved development plan.

issues.legal_issue: The legality of an exemption order need not be decided in a special leave proceeding when the High Court's review judgment is unchallenged and the petitioners' public-space concern has already been considered.
material_facts: The petitioners challenged a government order exempting the disputed land under the Urban Land (Ceiling and Regulation) Act, 1976.
The High Court considered the exemption challenge when disposing of review applications, but the petitioners did not challenge that review judgment.
The petitioners' stated concern was whether sufficient land remained reserved for a park or recreation ground, and the High Court had considered that concern.
issues.conclusion: The Court declined to decide the legality of the exemption order and dismissed the special leave petition.
issues.legal_principle: The Court held that it was not called upon to decide the exemption order's legality because the High Court had considered the grounds in its review judgment, that judgment was not challenged, and the public-space concern had been adequately considered.

predicates.exemption_order_challenged_in_special_le: A special leave proceeding challenged an order exempting land from a land-ceiling regime.
predicates.high_court_review_judgment_not_challenge: The party did not challenge the High Court judgment disposing of its review application.
predicates.public_open_space_concern_already_consid: The question whether sufficient land was reserved for public open space had already been considered by the High Court.

issues.definition: When an exemption order is challenged in a special leave proceeding, the relevant High Court review judgment is unchallenged, and the public open-space concern has already been considered, the Court declines to decide the exemption's legality.
